components.name: Map Tabs
components.description: Toolbar rail for switching maps; the current map is the one solid blue element in the chrome.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 3px; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--bg-primary, #0b0e14); border: 1px solid var(--border-color, #262e42); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Inter, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-tab { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 5px 11px; border: none; border-radius: 7px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-secondary, #94a3b8); font: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s ease; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--text-primary, #e6edf3); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); } .ds-tab--active { background: var(--accent-color, #3b82f6); color: #ffffff; } .ds-tab--active:hover { background: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; } .ds-tab-count { font-size: 10.5px; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14); }

components.name: Ghost Button

components.name: Trio Card
components.description: What / why / problem cards at the top of a node's detail panel; the heart of the reading experience.
components.html:
What
Promise-based ORM for Node.js that works with SQL databases.
Why
Define tables as models and query them with JS objects instead of raw SQL.
Problem
Raw SQL is verbose, error-prone, and disconnected from application code.
components.css: .ds-trio { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; width: 398px; max-width: 100%; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Inter, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-trio-card { padding: 11px 13px; border-radius: 9px; background: var(--bg-card, #161b28); border: 1px solid var(--border-color, #262e42); border-left-width: 3px; } .ds-trio-card--what { border-left-color: #3b82f6; } .ds-trio-card--why { border-left-color: #22c55e; } .ds-trio-card--problem { border-left-color: #f59e0b; } .ds-trio-label { font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--text-muted, #64748b); margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-trio-text { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--text-primary, #e6edf3); }

narrative.overview:
The graph is the map and the cards are the margin notes. The canvas gives you the territory: categories as tinted regions, technologies as labelled pins, relations as roads. The detail panel is where you stop and read what you wrote. Reading matters as much as navigating, so the card's what / why / problem trio and its code example get the calmest, most legible treatment in the app.

The mood is calm and focused, precise and honest, and a little friendly. It is calm because the chrome stays in slate and navy and only content carries saturated colour. It is precise because every hue, border style and opacity encodes a fact about a node: its status, its category, whether it lives on another map. It is friendly because of the soft corners, emoji kind icons and small hover lifts, so that a recruiter opening a shared link meets something approachable rather than an IDE.

Density is high but not cramped. Small type (11–13px), tight 4–12px gaps and three docked panes make a laptop screen hold a whole map. The canvas sits on a quiet dot grid, and everything floats over it at clearly separated depths.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, built on four navy steps from Margin Navy to Raised Navy.
Saturated colour only where it means something: the five statuses, content-defined category hues, selection and validation results.
Dashed lines mean distance: a node you haven't touched yet, or one whose home is another map.
Monospace marks identifiers: ids, tags, keyboard hints, code.
Soft, tactile controls: rounded corners at every scale, visible hover feedback, small lifts.

rules.name: The Facts-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour appears only where it encodes a fact: a status, a category, the current selection, or a validation result. Everything else is navy and slate.

rules.name: The Dashed-Means-Distance Rule
rules.body: A dashed border means the node is not yours yet (`planned`) or lives on another map (ghost node or ghost group). Nothing else is dashed.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Identifiers Rule
rules.body: Anything the user could type or paste (an id, a tag, a shortcut, a code sample, a validation message) is set in mono. Names and prose never are.

rules.name: The Quiet Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for small Ink Muted section labels and canvas group titles. Never uppercase a name, a button or a sentence.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it's docked, it's flat. A shadow says "this is above the map": nodes, the detail panel, overlaid panes, modals, banners. Cards inside a panel never cast one.

rules.name: The Translucent Overlay Rule
rules.body: Anything laid directly over the canvas (info pill, empty state, modal backdrop) is navy at 72–94% opacity with a 4–8px backdrop blur, so the map stays faintly visible underneath.

dos: **Do** encode status through the node's border colour, its pill badge and its legend dot together, using the five fixed status tokens.
**Do** use a category's hue only as a mark: the 5px node bar, its label text, its dot and its group frame tints.
**Do** show active and selected controls with Annotation Wash, an Annotation Blue border and Annotation Blue Light text. Reserve solid Annotation Blue for the current map tab and primary buttons.
**Do** separate docked surfaces by navy tone and 1px Border Navy lines, and give a shadow only to things that float (see The Float-Only Shadow Rule).
**Do** set ids, tags, keyboard hints, code and validation messages in the mono stack.
**Do** keep transitions short and eased (120–250ms) and limit movement to the 1px node lift.
**Do** give every new rounded element a corner from the existing scale (4/6/7/8/9/10/12/14/pill), stepping up with its size.
donts: **Don't** use a status hue for decoration or for a meaning other than its status. Status colours state facts about the author's experience.
**Don't** use a dashed border for anything except planned nodes and ghost nodes or groups (see The Dashed-Means-Distance Rule).
**Don't** put a shadow on cards or rows inside a docked panel.
**Don't** fill large surfaces with Annotation Blue or any saturated hue. The error banner is the only full-colour surface.
**Don't** make new design decisions that depend on the emoji icons; they are placeholders for an SVG set.
**Don't** hard-code new category colours in CSS or components. They belong in `content/maps.yaml`.
